description: Local overrides layered on top of the org-inherited Renovate config: group non-major updates per ecosystem to stop the per-manifest PR pileup, and automerge the safe tiers once CI is green. Major and pre-1.0 (0.x) updates stay separate for manual review.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Group security updates. For majors: drop packageFileDir from the group key so a single dep bumped across all 5 language frontends lands in ONE PR instead of five. The three lockstep sets (vite+@vitejs/plugin-react, react-router-dom+@grafana/faro-react+@grafana/faro-web-tracing, and any PyPI opentelemetry-* package) map to the SAME group name their non-security partners use in packageRules below — vulnerabilityAlerts force-overrides packageRules for security branches, so the security-flagged member must resolve its group name here to share a branch with its partners' bump. The opentelemetry-* check runs before the isMajor branch because that packageRule groups every update type, not just majors — a non-major security alert on a PyPI OTel package needs the same 'python opentelemetry' group as its unaffected companions, or it splits into 'pip_requirements security non-major' and recreates the unresolvable partial bump. Gated on datasource == pypi: 'opentelemetry-' also matches Ruby (Bundler) and Maven package names in this repo, which must NOT be pulled into the Python group. The generic major-security fallback is keyed on {datasource, depNameSanitized} rather than depNameSanitized alone, for the same cross-ecosystem reason — this repo has same-named packages (mysql2, pg) in both npm and Rubygems, which would otherwise collide into one branch and let an unrelated ecosystem's failure block both remediations. NOTE: vulnerabilityFixStrategy is NOT set here, on purpose — this top-level block has no per-package matcher, so setting 'highest' here would flip every ecosystem's (Go/Java/Node/Ruby too) security fixes from Renovate's 'lowest CVE-clearing version' default to 'highest available version', a much larger auto-merged jump than intended. It's nested instead inside the python-opentelemetry packageRule below (as its own vulnerabilityAlerts.vulnerabilityFixStrategy override), which IS matchable, so it only applies to that lockstep set.
vulnerabilityAlerts.groupName: {{#if (and (containsString depName "opentelemetry-") (equals datasource "pypi"))}}python opentelemetry{{else}}{{#if isMajor}}{{#if (or (equals depName "vite") (equals depName "@vitejs/plugin-react"))}}frontend vite + plugin-react{{else}}{{#if (or (equals depName "react-router-dom") (or (equals depName "@grafana/faro-react") (equals depName "@grafana/faro-web-tracing")))}}frontend react-router + faro-react{{else}}{{{datasource}}} {{{depNameSanitized}}} security major{{/if}}{{/if}}{{else}}{{{manager}}} security non-major{{/if}}{{/if}}

packageRules.description: Group Go non-major updates into one PR (all share go/.../services/go.mod+go.sum).
Group Python non-major updates into one PR.
Group Java/Maven non-major updates into one PR.
Group Ruby/Bundler non-major updates into one PR.
Group Node.js/npm non-major updates into one PR.
Group container base-image non-major updates into one PR.

Automerge the safe tiers (minor/patch/digest/pin) once branch checks pass — covers security patch/minor too. 0.x deps are pulled into a separate manual group by the rule below (applied after this one), so a single 0.x dep no longer blocks automerge of an ecosystem's non-0.x group. Requires the branch-protection ruleset to allow the Renovate app to bypass required review (see PR description).

Split pre-1.0 (0.x) non-major updates into their own per-ecosystem group and require manual review. SemVer permits breaking changes in 0.x minor releases (Renovate warns about this), and this repo has many 0.x deps (e.g. OpenTelemetry packages); a separate group lets the non-0.x members of each ecosystem still automerge via the rule above. Uses the plain /^0/ matcher (not a negated one) for broad Renovate-version compatibility.
Never automerge major updates; keep them separate and flag for manual review (potential breaking changes).

Cap setuptools below v82. This repo pins setuptools only to provide pkg_resources for opentelemetry-instrumentation (python:3.12-slim no longer bundles it); setuptools removed pkg_resources in v82, so any >=82 bump breaks the Python services at import time (see closed PR #23). Remove this cap if the otel bootstrap migrates off pkg_resources to importlib.metadata.

Lockstep: vite and @vitejs/plugin-react must bump together on majors. @vitejs/plugin-react's peerDependencies.vite trails vite by a major (e.g. plugin-react v4 peers vite ^4||^5), so bumping vite alone breaks npm's peer-dep resolution (ERESOLVE) at docker build. Grouping both into one major PR — across all 5 language frontends — lets them move together. Placed after the major rule so it keeps automerge:false + needs-manual-review while overriding only the group name; mirrors the vulnerabilityAlerts group so a security-triggered vite major joins the plugin-react major in the same branch.

Lockstep: react-router-dom, @grafana/faro-react, and @grafana/faro-web-tracing must bump together on majors. Faro's peerDependencies.react-router-dom and its ReactRouterVersion enum track the router major (faro-react 1.x peers react-router-dom ^4||^5||^6 and has no V7 enum), so bumping the router alone silently breaks Faro route instrumentation — core to this repo's demo. faro-web-tracing is included too: the app imports TracingInstrumentation from it directly, faro-react's major depends on the matching web-tracing major, and PR #62 upgraded all three together manually — a branch that bumps only the router + faro-react would leave the directly-imported tracing package on its old major, running two Faro/OpenTelemetry stacks side by side. Groups all three into one major PR across all 5 language frontends. NOTE: the bump still needs a manual frontend/src/faro.js change (ReactRouterVersion.V6 -> V7) — hence needs-manual-review from the major rule above.

Lockstep: the Python OpenTelemetry SDK/exporter (1.x, e.g. opentelemetry-sdk) and the instrumentation packages (0.x beta, e.g. opentelemetry-instrumentation-flask) share a single opentelemetry-api and MUST bump together — opentelemetry-sdk 1.44 pins opentelemetry-api 1.44 while instrumentation 0.48b0 pins 1.27, so a partial bump is unresolvable (pip ResolutionImpossible). Without this rule the 1.x packages land in 'python non-major' and the 0.x ones in the '0.x manual review' group, producing two PRs that each fail to install. Group all opentelemetry-* pip packages into one manual-review PR so they move as a set. Placed after the 0.x rule so this groupName wins for the 0.x instrumentation packages too. ignoreUnstable:false is required here — Renovate's default (true) skips proposing beta releases like 0.65b0 for the still-0.x instrumentation packages, which silently drops them out of this group and recreates the same unresolvable partial bump this rule exists to prevent (confirmed via a Renovate dry-run: without this flag the instrumentation packages get updates: [] while the SDK/exporter alone move to 1.44.0). The nested vulnerabilityAlerts.vulnerabilityFixStrategy:highest below scopes that setting to just this lockstep set (vulnerabilityFixStrategy's only allowed parent is vulnerabilityAlerts, and the top-level vulnerabilityAlerts block has no per-package matcher, so setting it there would leak to every ecosystem's security fixes) — an alerted OTel package then moves to the SAME release family as its pinned companions instead of just the minimal CVE fix. matchPackageNames uses an unanchored /opentelemetry-/ regex (not /^opentelemetry-/) to match the containsString check the vulnerabilityAlerts groupName template above uses for grouping — an anchored regex here would let a hypothetical package like flask-opentelemetry-shim get routed into the 'python opentelemetry' branch by vulnerabilityAlerts while silently missing this rule's automerge:false/needs-manual-review protections.
